EXPERIENCE
Sunrise Bakery | Assistant Store Manager | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Managed opening shifts and a team of 6 bakers and cashiers, keeping the store within its weekly labour budget.
- Ran daily stock counts and supplier orders, cutting unsold bread from 12% to 7% of production.
Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Improved risk-adjusted returns by 35% with a cost-aware position smoother on the desk's futures signal.
- Validated the signal on 6 years of tick data with purged walk-forward splits and an embargo period, so every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
- Wrote a feature store for 120 microstructure features with point-in-time joins, which the research team reused in two later signal projects.
- Presented the signal, its capacity estimate and failure cases to the portfolio managers, who approved a small live allocation for the next quarter.
- Selected the smoother's parameters from 400 backtested configurations and reported the best one's Sharpe as the expected live Sharpe.
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Jun 2020 - Aug 2021
- Cut a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours by running the runs in parallel with the same random seed on every worker.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator; my proof tightens the previous bound by a log factor and is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability, writing 12 problem sets and earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.
- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation with shrinkage and factor models, downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Beat a HAR-RV baseline's out-of-sample QLIKE loss by 7% on 30 equity indices with a temporal convolutional model trained on realized-volatility features.
- Tested significance with Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices; after a Holm correction the forecast gain held at the 5% level on 24 of them and in both crisis periods.
- Wrote up the method, robustness checks and results as a 12-page working paper, which was presented at the department's financial econometrics seminar.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Engineered features and trained gradient-boosting models for a market prediction competition.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Added 0.4 to the Sharpe ratio of a futures book with an order-book imbalance signal, tested over 18 months out of sample.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch, Kafka
Methods: time-series econometircs, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: The best Sharpe from 400 backtested configurations cannot be reported as the expected live Sharpe.
items.because: Selecting the maximum creates multiple-testing and selection bias, making it an optimistically selected backtest statistic.

items.says: The 0.4 Sharpe change is not labeled as an absolute or relative increase or tied to comparison values.
items.because: The missing values and unclear comparison prevent a reader from judging the performance.

items.says: Sunrise Bakery appears before the quantitative experience and projects.
items.because: An unrelated role dominates the career story for a recruiter scanning for quantitative work.

items.says: Staying within the weekly labour budget does not show the scale or business value of the control.
items.because: Without a comparison, the outcome could be routine compliance rather than meaningful efficiency.

items.says: “Ran daily stock counts and supplier orders” does not identify the inventory decision and makes orders sound as though they were run.
items.because: The wording shows routine activity but obscures the operational judgment and the candidate’s role in ordering.

items.says: The line attributes the reduction in unsold bread to stock counts and supplier orders without establishing causation.
items.because: Other changes could explain the reduction without consistent measurements and evidence linking it to ordering.

items.says: The 35% risk-adjusted-return improvement lacks a defined metric, baseline, period and validation status.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what was compared or whether the figure is an out-of-sample result or a selected backtest estimate.

items.says: Purged walk-forward splits and an embargo do not establish that every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
items.because: They do not automatically make feature construction, preprocessing, labels or parameter selection point-in-time.

items.says: The six-year validation describes the research process without stating its outcome or decision.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether the signal survived validation or what evidence supported deployment.

items.says: The 400-configuration search describes the research process without stating a validated outcome or decision it enabled.
items.because: The bullet emphasizes effort rather than evidence supporting deployment or performance.

items.says: The feature-store bullet puts implementation details before the result that two later projects reused it.
items.because: Readers scanning the bullet may notice the technical activity before the evidence of adoption.

items.says: The presentation bullet puts the live-allocation result after the presentation details.
items.because: The consequential deployment outcome has less immediate impact.

items.says: “Approved a small live allocation” leaves the size of the deployment unspecified.
items.because: “Small” does not let a reader judge the deployment’s scale or what the capacity estimate demonstrated.

items.says: Northpeak repeats the same type of Sharpe improvement within its own bullets.
items.because: The repeated performance story takes space from distinct evidence of research impact.

items.says: The order-book signal achievement appears under both Northpeak and the Kaggle project.
items.because: The apparent same book, period and signal may make a reader count one achievement twice or doubt its provenance.

items.says: Using the same random seed on every worker does not provide valid independent Monte Carlo replications.
items.because: Duplicated or overlapping pseudorandom streams would invalidate the study’s uncertainty estimates.

items.says: “Running the runs in parallel” is repetitive wording.
items.because: A direct description of parallel execution would state the runtime achievement more clearly.

items.says: “My proof” breaks the résumé’s phrase-based format.
items.because: The first-person pronoun adds no ownership information and is inconsistent with surrounding bullets.

items.says: “Tightens the previous bound by a log factor” does not give the compared bounds or exact improvement.
items.because: A reader cannot tell how substantial the mathematical contribution is.

items.says: The teaching outcome gives a rating but no educational impact.
items.because: Student satisfaction does not show whether students learned more or performed better.

items.says: The 7% QLIKE improvement is not identified as relative or a percentage-point difference.
items.because: The reader cannot interpret the size of the gain precisely.

items.says: The line does not establish whether the crisis-period tests were included in the Holm correction.
items.because: Correcting the index tests does not automatically control error rates for additional crisis-period tests.

items.says: “Both crisis periods” does not identify the periods tested.
items.because: Their names or dates would make the robustness claim assessable.

items.says: The working-paper bullet lists broad contents without identifying a specific analytical contribution.
items.because: It does not show what research skill the writing demonstrates beyond the earlier modeling and testing bullets.

items.says: The feature-engineering bullet gives no competition result and repeats the heading’s context.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether the models improved a baseline or earned a meaningful score or rank.

items.says: Switching to time-grouped folds does not by itself prove that leakage caused or eliminated the 0.02 gap.
items.because: The method change alone does not establish the causal mechanism or show that the gap was closed.

items.says: The 0.02 gap lacks a scoring metric and is not identified as an absolute score difference.
items.because: A reader cannot judge its size or meaning without knowing what was scored and how the gap was calculated.

items.says: The futures-book result lacks a clearly distinguished comparison portfolio and before-and-after Sharpe ratios.
items.because: A reader cannot tell how the 0.4 change was calculated or whether it is the Northpeak result.

items.says: The final Kaggle bullet introduces a separate futures-signal achievement after two bullets about a leakage-control modeling workflow.
items.because: The shift makes the project hard to understand as one contribution and leaves its connection to the competition unclear.

items.says: “Econometircs” is misspelled.
items.because: The misspelling can undermine confidence in technical care and interfere with keyword matching.

items.says: Kafka is listed without any résumé entry showing its use.
items.because: A reader cannot verify the skill or see what level of work it represents.
